question.problem:
A point is chosen uniformly at random from the interval $[0,1].$ Let the continuous random variable $X$ be the distance from the origin to the chosen point. Consider the triangle with vertices at $(0,0),(X,0),$ and $(X,2X).$ Let $A=A(X)$ denote the area of this triangle.

Expressing the integrand in the following equation as a polynomial, we have 

$E[A]={\int }_{0}^{1}$
{{field-1}} $dx$

Therefore, the expected area of the triangle is 
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x)$, the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(x)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\text{ }\text{d}x,
$$

where $f(x)$ is the probability density function of $X.$ 

In this problem, $X$ is chosen uniformly from $[0,1]$, so the probability density function is

$$
f(x)=1,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\le x<1.
$$

Let $A$ denote the area of the triangle formed by the three points $(0,0),(X,0),$ and $(X,2X).$ The triangle has a base of length $X$ along the $x$-axis from $(0,0)$ to $(X,0)$, and a height of length $2X$ from $(X,0)$ to $(X,2X).$ Using the standard formula for the area of a triangle, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base}\cdot \text{height} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot X\cdot 2X \\  & ={X}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, we define

$$
r(x)={x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[A] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
